title: Blues in 1918 and the origin of the Bugle Blues
summary: He says many men sang blues in 1918, credits Jim Europe's band with the Bugle Blues not Benny Goodman, and compares Southern and Western blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Now, around 1918 in Atlantic City. There were a lot of singers there, and you played for some of them. Did any of them sing blues, had that come in yet.

In fact, at that time, there was quite a lot of singers, and a lot of men sang the blues. At that time. At that time, you'll find out that -- 1918 -- of course that, someone said the other night was all wrong, said Benny

Goodman, said he did the "Bugle Blues". Well, that wasn't so. Jim Muir started the Bugle Blues in Europe, in 1917, during the war. See, one of his trumpets would play, (imitates trumpet), they did that in 1917, before Benny was born.
So whoever said that was incorrect.
Now, we had a blues, but it was different types of blues. We had the blues coming from the South, was a little different from the Western blues.

Well, it was slower, and -- well, it was all blues, all twelve bars, like that, it was all blues, but there seemed to be more of a wail coming from North Carolina and Virginia and Georgia and like that. The guys would walk along the railroad track. They used to sing songs like, "Honey Let Your DRAWERS Hang Low", you see.

(sings) "La de de de dah, dah, dah. La de de de dah, dah, dah. Was the last time you're going to shake it in the sheets with me." You see what I mean, those old low down blues. But in the West, it was a different type of blues. It was a blues -- were built more up. Because Chicago surpassed New York, in bands. And so did Detroit. Because they had big bands when we only had two and three pieces, you know? So

that's the reason why they got a better grip on the music. And a lot of the best jazz musicians would come from -- and Ohio was another place. Ohio, Toledo in Ohio, and Columbus, they had musicians. And Detroit, and Chicago. St. Louis, they had musicians on their instruments long before we had them in New York.
